title: Lambda/Function Invocation Volume Trending

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.6.2 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.6.2 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch` collected via Splunk Add-on for AWS (CloudWatch metrics), Azure Monitor; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: Splunk Add-on for AWS (CloudWatch metrics), Azure Monitor
spl:
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" Namespace="AWS/Lambda" MetricName="Invocations"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.6.2_lambda_function_invocati_2"
| sort -_time
description: Daily invocation counts show traffic growth, seasonal patterns, and the impact of new features or batch jobs. Sharp changes often precede cost spikes or throttling if concurrency limits are fixed.
value: Detecting lambda/function invocation volume trending early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable CloudWatch metric ingestion for AWS/Lambda Invocations with FunctionName dimension. For Azure, use Microsoft.Web/sites/functions equivalent metrics. Normalize time to UTC for daily buckets. Use top-N functions by volume to keep the chart readable. Correlate step changes with deployments from CI/CD timestamps.
visualization: Line chart (daily invocations with 7-day SMA, 30 days), column chart (top functions by volume).
knownFalsePositives: Cold starts, retries, and a bad client sending junk traffic can all raise error counts without a code bug. We look at the share of invocations and we compare the same time last week before we assume the function is broken.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure Splunk Add-on for AWS (CloudWatch metrics), Azure Monitor with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.6.7.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `metric_name` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable CloudWatch metric ingestion for AWS/Lambda Invocations with FunctionName dimension. For Azure, use Microsoft.Web/sites/functions equivalent metrics. Normalize time to UTC for daily buckets. Use top-N functions by volume to keep the chart readable. Correlate step changes with deployments from CI/CD timestamps.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" Namespace="AWS/Lambda" MetricName="Invocations"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.6.2_lambda_function_invocati_2"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch` in `index=cloud` to detect lambda/function invocation volume trending. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon CloudWatch console Metrics for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `metric_name` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_6_2_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (daily invocations with 7-day SMA, 30 days), column chart (top functions by volume)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Add-on for AWS (CloudWatch metrics), Azure Monitor and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of lambda/function invocation volume trending so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
